UPSTREAM: drm/amdgpu: Switch baremetal to use KIQ for compute ring management. (v3) KIQ is the Kernel Interface Queue for managing the MEC. Rather than setting up rings via direct MMIO of ring registers, the rings are configured via special packets sent to the KIQ. The allows the MEC to better manage shared resources and certain power events. v2: squash in s3/s4 fix from Rex v3: further fixes from Rex BUG=b:66735140 TEST=boot Kahlee, run graphics_SanAngeles Signed-off-by: David Panariti <David.Panariti@amd.com> Reviewed-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> Acked-by: Tom St Denis <tom.stdenis@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> (cherry picked from commit b4e40676e4aade3141194617199bec77a32b5680) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: Idbad4c961f827489c274233543a6c63d80f5f7ec Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/729647 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: Documentation/devicetree: Add pcie-reset-suspend property The patch is self-descriptive. I've found that we may need platform-specific behavior for the PERST# signal in system suspend, depending on the type of PCIe endpoints are attached. Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10002877/) BUG=b:65559913 TEST=observe WAKE# pin on scarlet Change-Id: I76e2835addad922453ef7ac99994d58d5bfe3c00 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/717451 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: of/pci: Add of_pci_get_pcie_reset_suspend() to parse pcie-reset-suspend This helper can be used by drivers to determine the expected PERST# behavior when in low-power system suspend (e.g., S3). I've found the expected behavior to vary across a few different endpoint implementations. Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10002875/) BUG=b:65559913 TEST=observe WAKE# pin on scarlet Change-Id: I07b95430df241f0fc2cbe5a0f70f5550ea217a18 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/717452 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: PCI: rockchip: Support configuring PERST# state via DT I've found that different endpoints and board configurations have required different behavior from the PCIe Reset (PERST#) signal when in low-power system suspend (e.g., S3). Use the new of_pci helper to request this state and assert (active low) PERST# before suspending. Note that we reinitialize the link (including reconfiguring PERST#) at resume time. This requires that the board and system firmware supports driving this signal low when the system is suspended, since PERST# may be pulled up by the endpoint, and some GPIO banks are not active in S3. Signed-off-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10002883/) BUG=b:65559913 TEST=observe WAKE# pin on scarlet Change-Id: I61212a46b12276e0c92d92d6cf478b04d29943b1 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/717453 Commit-Ready: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Tested-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: rockchip: Assert PERST# in S3 on scarlet With QCA Wifi, it's expected that we assert PERST# when suspending the system, to ensure lower power and to enable WAKE# (Wake-on-WLAN).
